mainTopic: The end of the story of רבי יהושע בן חנניה and the elders of Athens, the משנה about פטר חמור with twin births, and the גמרא's proof that this משנה does not follow רבי יוסי הגלילי.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a story. רבי יהושע בן חנניה brings the captured elders of Athens before the emperor and proves they are the real elders by throwing their home soil on them. He then defeats them with water from a spot in the sea that swallows everything. Next, a new משנה teaches how much a donkey owner gives the כהן for פטר חמור when there are twin births and it is unclear which baby came out first. The rule is that only a male who is certainly a firstborn obligates a lamb. When it is in doubt, the owner sets a lamb aside but keeps it, because the כהן cannot prove his claim. The משנה also teaches that the redemption lamb has no holiness and can be any sheep or goat. The גמרא then asks whether the משנה could follow רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds that two births can happen at exactly the same moment. אביי tries to fit the משנה to him, but a ברייתא shows רבי יוסי הגלילי applies his rule to donkeys too. So אביי is refuted, and the משנה follows the חכמים.

steps.title: Collecting water from the swallowing place
steps.stepSummary: On the way back, רבי יהושע בן חנניה fills a small jug with water from בי בליעי.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they reached the 'House of the Swallowed,' he filled a small jug with water from there.
steps.whatsHappening: The story keeps going. רבי יהושע quietly collects special water that he will use later in the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בי בליעי is a spot in the sea that swallows up whatever is near it. The jug of water is a setup. It will become the tool he uses to defeat the elders at the end.

keyTerms.meaning: 'House of the Swallowed', a place in the sea that swallows everything

phrases.english: When they reached the House of the Swallowed,
phrases.notes: This is a spot in the sea where the water sucks in everything around it.

phrases.english: he filled a small jug of water from the House of the Swallowed.
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יהושע בן חנניה, who is bringing the elders of Athens back as captives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative detail: רבי יהושע takes water from בי בליעי.

steps.title: The emperor doubts these are the real elders
steps.stepSummary: The elders arrive before the קיסר looking weak, so he doubts they are the famous sages of Athens.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they arrived, he stood them before the emperor. The emperor saw they were miserable and said: These are not them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע presents his captives to the קיסר. The emperor refuses to believe these broken men are the proud elders of Athens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The elders were known for being strong and arrogant. Being captives made them humble and quiet, so the emperor thinks רבי יהושע brought the wrong people. This sets up the next move, where רבי יהושע proves who they are.

phrases.english: When they arrived, he stood them before the emperor.
He saw that they were suffering,
phrases.notes: The emperor is the one who sees how beaten down they look.

phrases.english: He said to him: These are not them.
phrases.notes: He means these can't be the famous proud sages of Athens.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next scene in the story: arriving before the emperor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative: the emperor doubts the identity of the captives.

steps.title: Their home soil brings back their arrogance
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע throws Athenian earth on them. They become arrogant again, and the emperor hands them over to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He took some of their earth and threw it on them, and they spoke harshly before the king. The emperor said to him: Do whatever you want with them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע proves these are the real elders. He throws some of their own country's dirt on them, and they go back to their proud, rude selves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Smelling their home soil gave them back their old attitude, and they acted arrogantly right in front of the king. That convinced the emperor, so he gave רבי יהושע full permission to deal with them.

keyTerms.meaning: they became hard, they acted arrogantly

phrases.english: He took some of their earth and threw it on them,
phrases.notes: This is dirt from Athens, their own homeland, that רבי יהושע had brought along.

phrases.english: and they acted harshly before the king.
phrases.notes: Literally 'they became hard', meaning they spoke with arrogance.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כֹּל דְּבָעֵית עֲבֵיד בְּהוּ.
phrases.english: He said to him: Whatever you want, do with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the emperor's doubt from Step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative: the elders are proven genuine and handed over to רבי יהושע.

steps.title: The impossible task: fill the vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע pours the swallowing water into a vessel and tells the elders they can go free once they fill it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brought the water from the House of the Swallowed, poured it into a vessel, and said to them: Fill it up, then go on your way.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע sets a final challenge. The elders may leave once they fill the vessel. This sets up the ending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water from בי בליעי swallows whatever comes near it. That means anything poured into this vessel will disappear. The task sounds easy, but it is really impossible.

phrases.english: He brought the water that he had brought from the House of the Swallowed,
poured it into a vessel,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: מַלְיוּהּ לְהוּ וְאֵיזִילוּ לְכוּ.
phrases.english: he said to them: Fill it up, and go on your way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the permission from Step 3 and the water from Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative: the elders are given an impossible task.

steps.title: The elders wear themselves out and are defeated
steps.stepSummary: Every pour is swallowed up. The elders keep pouring until their shoulders give out, and they are finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: They filled and poured in, one after another, and it swallowed it up. They kept filling until their shoulders came out of joint, and they wore out and were finished.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. The vessel swallows all the water, so the elders exhaust themselves and are defeated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each time they poured, the water vanished, just as the water of בי בליעי does. They kept going until their bodies broke down. That is the end of רבי יהושע's contest with the elders of Athens.

keyTerms.meaning: one after another, again and again
their shoulders slipped out of place

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע בן חנניה defeats the elders of Athens using their own arrogance (the soil) and the swallowing water from בי בליעי.

phrases.english: They filled and poured into it, one after another,
and it swallowed them up,
they kept filling until their shoulders slipped out of joint,
and they wore out and were finished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the result of the task set in Step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The elders of Athens are defeated by the endlessly swallowing water.

steps.title: One donkey gives birth to twins
steps.stepSummary: A first-time mother donkey has twins. With two males, the owner gives one lamb to the כהן. With a male and a female, he sets a lamb aside but keeps it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A female donkey that never gave birth before had two males: he gives one lamb to the כהן. A male and a female: he sets aside one lamb for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, about redeeming a firstborn donkey (פטר חמור) with a lamb. It covers what happens when one donkey has twins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two males, one of them is surely the firstborn, so the כהן gets a lamb. With a male and a female, maybe the female came out first, and then there is no פטר חמור. The owner still sets aside a lamb because of the doubt. But the כהן cannot prove he is owed it, so the owner keeps it.

keyTerms.meaning: firstborn male donkey, redeemed with a lamb

steps.confusionAlert: 'Sets aside one lamb for himself' does not mean he owes nothing at all. He must designate the lamb because of the doubt, but he gets to keep it, since the כהן cannot prove the male was born first.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic rule of money claims: when it is uncertain, the one who wants to take money from someone else has to bring proof.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: A female donkey that had not given birth before
and gave birth to two males —
he gives one lamb to the priest,
a male and a female —
he sets aside one lamb for himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲמוֹרָה שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרָה וְיָלְדָה שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה; unrelated to the story before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two males: one lamb to the כהן. Male and female: a lamb is set aside but stays with the owner.

steps.title: Two donkeys each have a male
steps.stepSummary: If two first-time donkeys give birth to two males, both are firstborn, so the owner gives two lambs.
steps.simpleTranslation: His two donkeys that never gave birth before had two males: he gives two lambs to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a case with two mother donkeys.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each donkey is having her first baby, and both babies are male. So both are certainly פטר חמור, and there is nothing in doubt.

phrases.english: His two donkeys that had not given birth before
and they gave birth to two males —
he gives two lambs to the priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתֵּי חֲמוֹרָיו שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרוּ וְיָלְדוּ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands from one mother donkey to two.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two donkeys, two males: two lambs to the כהן.

steps.title: Cases where one male is surely firstborn
steps.stepSummary: Male and female, or two males and a female: one lamb goes to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A male and a female, or two males and a female: he gives one lamb to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists mixed births from two donkeys where at least one male must be a firstborn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two mothers, there are two firstborns. If the births were a male and a female, each donkey had one baby, so the male is certainly a firstborn. If there were two males and a female, at least one of the two firstborns has to be a male. Either way, exactly one lamb is certainly owed.

phrases.aramaic: זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה, אוֹ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים וּנְקֵבָה —
phrases.english: A male and a female, or two males and a female —
he gives one lamb to the priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה, אוֹ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים וּנְקֵבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next case in the two-donkey list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When at least one male is certainly a firstborn, one lamb is given.

steps.title: Cases where the כהן gets nothing
steps.stepSummary: Two females and a male, or two males and two females: the כהן receives nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two females and a male, or two males and two females: the כהן gets nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with the cases where no male is certainly a firstborn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In these cases, it is possible that both firstborns were the females. Since no male is surely a firstborn, the כהן cannot prove he is owed anything.
steps.whatToRemember: The כהן only gets a lamb for a male that is certainly a firstborn. When it is in doubt, he cannot take the lamb from the owner.

phrases.english: Two females and a male,
or two males and two females —
the priest gets nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתֵּי נְקֵבוֹת וְזָכָר, אוֹ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים וּשְׁתֵּי נְקֵבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final cases of the list, the opposite of Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the firstborns could both be females, the כהן receives nothing.

steps.title: One experienced donkey and one first-time donkey give birth
steps.stepSummary: If one donkey had given birth before and one had not, and together they produce two males, the owner gives one lamb to the כהן. If they produce a male and a female, he sets aside one lamb and keeps it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One donkey had already given birth before and one had not. If they gave birth to two males, he gives one lamb to the כהן. If a male and a female, he sets aside one lamb for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more twin-birth case to its list: one donkey is a first-time mother and the other is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two males, one of them must have come from the first-time mother, so one lamb definitely goes to the כהן. With a male and a female, the male might belong to the donkey that already gave birth, so it is a ספק. He sets aside a lamb but keeps it, because the כהן cannot take something without proof (המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה).

keyTerms.meaning: She already gave birth before, so her next baby is not a בכור
A lamb, used to redeem the firstborn donkey
For himself; the owner keeps it

steps.confusionAlert: בִּיכְּרָה here means she already gave birth before. So the donkey that 'ביכרה' is the one whose baby is NOT a בכור. It is easy to read it backwards.

phrases.english: One had already given birth before,
phrases.notes: This is about two donkeys owned by the same person. This one's baby cannot be a firstborn.

phrases.english: and one had never given birth before,
and they gave birth to two males —
he gives one lamb to the כהן;
if a male and a female —
he sets aside one lamb for himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of mixed twin-birth cases from steps 6–9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two males from a mixed pair means one lamb goes to the כהן. Male and female means a lamb is set aside but kept by the owner, because of the doubt.

steps.title: The verse for redeeming with a lamb and the laws of that lamb
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'ופטר חמור תפדה בשה' is the source. The lamb can be a sheep or a goat, male or female, old or young, unblemished or blemished, and it can be used many times. A lamb the owner keeps is ordinary property: it is tithed and may be used if it dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And the firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a שה.' It can be from sheep or goats, male or female, big or small, unblemished or blemished. One may redeem with it many times. It enters the pen to be tithed, and if it dies, one may benefit from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the פסוק behind redeeming a donkey with a lamb, then lists which lambs qualify and what status the lamb has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שה is broad, so any kind of sheep or goat works, including a blemished one. The lamb is not holy at all, so it can be reused for redemption again and again. A lamb kept because of a ספק is fully the owner's: it goes into מעשר בהמה like his other animals, and its carcass may be used.

keyTerms.meaning: The firstborn male of a donkey
You shall redeem it with a lamb or kid
One may get benefit from it

steps.whatToRemember: The redemption lamb has no holiness. Any שה works, it can be reused, and a lamb the owner keeps is regular property that gets tithed and can be used even after it dies.

phrases.english: As it is said: "And the firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb,"
phrases.notes: This פסוק is in שמות פרק ל״ד.

phrases.english: from the sheep or from the goats,
male or female, old or young,
unblemished or blemished,
he may redeem with it many times,
it enters the pen to be tithed,
phrases.notes: This refers to the lamb the owner kept because of the doubt. It is counted with his regular flock for מעשר בהמה.

phrases.english: and if it dies, one may benefit from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for the redemption lamb used in all the cases, and defines that lamb's status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any sheep or goat, of any kind, may serve as the redemption lamb. It has no holiness and is reusable, and a kept lamb is ordinary, tithable property.

steps.title: The גמרא asks who taught the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking which תנא is the author of the משנה's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: Who is the תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks whose opinion the משנה follows. It is setting up the next step, where רבי ירמיה answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the earlier case of a first-time donkey with two male twins, where only one lamb is given (step 6). The ruling assumes one twin came out first, so the גמרא wants to know which תנא holds that view.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא? (whose opinion is this?)

phrases.english: GEMARA: Who is the tanna (author of this ruling)?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the twin-males case earlier in the משנה, where only one lamb is given.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's analysis of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that when two male twins are born, only one of them is a בכור?

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: the משנה does not follow רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says the משנה cannot follow רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds that two births can happen at exactly the same moment. By his view, both twins would be firstborn and two lambs would be needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: It is not like רבי יוסי הגלילי. Because if it were רבי יוסי הגלילי, doesn't he say it is possible for two births to happen at exactly the same instant?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the question by ruling out one תנא, רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי holds אפשר לצמצם, meaning twins can come out at exactly the same moment, so both would be firstborn. Since the משנה gives only one lamb, it must follow the חכמים, who say one twin always comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: It is possible for two events to line up at exactly the same instant
Doesn't he say...? (pointing to his known view)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
It is not in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
because if it were Rabbi Yosei HaGelili —
doesn't he say it is possible for them to coincide exactly!
phrases.notes: He means the twins could come out at the very same moment, so both are firstborn and need two lambs. His view comes from a later משנה about kosher animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'מאן תנא' question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not רבי יוסי הגלילי, because his principle of אפשר לצמצם would make both twins firstborn, which would mean two lambs.

steps.title: אביי: even רבי יוסי הגלילי could agree here
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the משנה can follow רבי יוסי הגלילי after all. His view that both twins are firstborn comes from the plural word הזכרים, which is written only about kosher animals, not donkeys.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You can even say it follows רבי יוסי הגלילי. It is different there, because it is written, 'The males are to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רבי ירמיה's reasoning and shows the משנה could match רבי יוסי הגלילי too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה assumed רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule applies to every kind of firstborn. אביי says it is tied to the plural 'הזכרים', which is written about kosher animals. That פסוק teaches that two males can both be firstborn. For a donkey there is no such word, so only one twin is a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: "The males are to ה׳" — plural, about kosher firstborn animals

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ירמיה: the משנה is not רבי יוסי הגלילי. אביי: it can be, because his 'both are firstborn' rule comes from the plural הזכרים, which is said only about kosher animals and not about a donkey.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not say רבי יוסי הגלילי drops his principle of אפשר לצמצם. He says that for kosher animals the plural word teaches that both twins count, and that teaching does not carry over to donkeys.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
You can even say it is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
it is different there, because it is written: "The males are to the Lord."
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of a kosher animal. The פסוק is in שמות פרק י״ג, and the plural 'males' shows two can both be firstborn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי ירמיה's conclusion that the משנה excludes רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the משנה must go against רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי ירמיה assumed רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling applies to all firstborns. In fact it rests on the plural הזכרים, which is written only about kosher animals.

steps.title: Why not learn donkeys from kosher animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: even if הזכרים is written about kosher animals, donkeys should follow the same rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the law of the donkey be learned from the kosher animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging what אביי just said. If two kosher animals born together can both be firstborn, why not say the same for donkeys?
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the source for two firstborns is written only about kosher animals. The challenge is that one kind of בכור could teach us about the other, so the rule should carry over to a firstborn donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us learn from it, meaning copy the law from one case to another

phrases.english: But let it be learned from it!
phrases.notes: "It" is the kosher firstborn. The question is why the donkey shouldn't follow the same rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's limit on the source הזכרים
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the two-firstborn rule is limited to kosher animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Laws of one kind of בכור are often learned from another, so the rule should apply to donkeys as well.

steps.title: The Torah limited the rule to kosher animals
steps.stepSummary: The word הזכרים itself shows the Torah limited this rule, so donkeys cannot learn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Merciful One limited it with the word "the males."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The תורה itself limited this rule to the place where הזכרים is written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word that teaches that two animals can both be firstborn also shows that the rule stays in its own case. So a firstborn donkey cannot borrow it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
"The males", a plural word written about kosher firstborn animals

phrases.english: The Merciful One limited it with "the males."
phrases.notes: The verse is "הזכרים לה׳", "the males shall be the Lord's," said about kosher animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Donkeys could learn the two-firstborn rule from kosher animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word הזכרים keeps the rule limited to kosher animals.
steps.whatToRemember: At this point אביי's position stands: he says רבי יוסי הגלילי's two-firstborn rule is limited to kosher animals. Steps 19–23 will challenge this, and Step 23 refutes it.

steps.title: Second version: maybe the משנה does not follow רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: A second telling of the discussion suggests the משנה is not like רבי יוסי הגלילי, since he holds that two births can happen at exactly the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: Let us say the משנה is not like רבי יוסי הגלילי, because רבי יוסי הגלילי says it is possible for two births to happen at exactly the same moment!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives a second version of the same discussion. It opens by suggesting the משנה does not follow רבי יוסי הגלילי, and this sets up אביי's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is the same as רבי ירמיה's in step 13. In this version it is presented as an open suggestion. If two births can be perfectly at the same moment, twin donkeys could both be firstborn and need two lambs, but the משנה requires only one.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say, a suggestion that is being tested
It is possible to be exact, meaning two events can happen at precisely the same moment

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same disagreement retold in a slightly different form, which the גמרא marks with איכא דאמרי.

phrases.english: Some say:
Let us say it is not like Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
for if it were Rabbi Yosei HaGelili —
doesn't he say it is possible for it to be exact?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: לֵימָא דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts the discussion of steps 12–14 as a second version
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה can follow רבי יוסי הגלילי

steps.title: אביי: the משנה can still follow רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the משנה can follow רבי יוסי הגלילי, because his two-firstborn rule comes from הזכרים לה׳, which is about kosher animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You can even say it follows רבי יוסי הגלילי. It is different there, since it is written "the males shall be the Lord's."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes away the suggestion and says the משנה can follow רבי יוסי הגלילי after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling that both twins are firstborn depends on the verse הזכרים לה׳. That verse speaks of kosher animals, so for a donkey even he would require only one lamb.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
You can even say it is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
it is different there,
phrases.notes: "There" means the case of kosher animals, where רבי יוסי הגלילי rules that both are firstborn.

phrases.english: for it is written: "The males shall be the Lord's."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 17
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the משנה cannot match רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes his two-firstborn rule applies to donkeys, but it comes from a verse about kosher animals.

steps.title: Why doesn't the משנה mention both heads coming out together?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: if the משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, it should have stated the case of both heads emerging at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רבי ירמיה, who does not explain the משנה as רבי יוסי הגלילי. That is why it does not teach "and both their heads came out as one." But for אביי, let it teach "and both their heads came out as one"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's view by looking at what the משנה leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ירמיה, the משנה follows the חכמים, who say births can never be exactly at the same moment, so there is nothing to mention. For אביי, that case is possible and it is the biggest new point. The משנה should have said that even then only one lamb is given, so its silence is a problem for אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense for, the first half of a challenge that sets one view against another
Explains or places it, meaning the משנה, as following a certain view
And both their heads came out as one, meaning a truly simultaneous birth

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Yirmeya,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא מוֹקֵי לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי —
phrases.english: who does not explain it as Rabbi Yosei HaGelili —
that is why it does not teach
"and both their heads came out as one,"
phrases.notes: These words are used in another משנה where רבי יוסי הגלילי's view is taught.

phrases.english: but according to Abaye —
let it teach "and both their heads came out as one"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer in step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a simultaneous birth is possible, the משנה should have stated that case, since that is where the real new point would be.

steps.title: A ברייתא: רבי יוסי הגלילי gives both donkeys to the כהן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי יוסי הגלילי rules that twin donkeys whose heads emerged together both go to the כהן, using the verse הזכרים לה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, it is taught in a ברייתא: If someone's donkey had never given birth and it gave birth to two males, and both their heads came out as one, רבי יוסי הגלילי says: both of them go to the כהן, as it says "the males shall be the Lord's."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger challenge against אביי by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said רבי יוסי הגלילי uses הזכרים only for kosher animals. This ברייתא shows him applying the same verse to a firstborn donkey and requiring two lambs. That directly contradicts the claim that the משנה, which requires one lamb, can follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: Gave birth for the first time

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא seems to knock out the very distinction אביי relied on, which explains why רבי ירמיה refused to put the משנה with רבי יוסי הגלילי.

phrases.english: Furthermore, it is taught:
His donkey that had never given birth
and it gave birth to two males,
and both their heads came out as one,
Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
both of them go to the priest,
phrases.notes: He means the owner gives a lamb for each donkey, so the כהן gets two.

phrases.english: as it says: "The males shall be the Lord's."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to אביי alongside step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that רבי יוסי הגלילי applies הזכרים only to kosher animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows רבי יוסי הגלילי applying הזכרים to donkeys, so a משנה that requires only one lamb cannot follow him.

steps.title: But that verse is about animals with built-in holiness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא could use הזכרים לה׳ for donkeys, since that verse is written about kosher firstborns, which have קדושת הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when this verse is written, isn't it written about an animal that has built-in holiness?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses on the ברייתא from Step 20 and asks how it could use this verse for donkeys at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse הזכרים לה׳ talks about a kosher בכור, which is itself holy and is brought on the מזבח. A פטר חמור has no holiness of its own. It is only redeemed. So it seems strange to take a rule from a holy animal and apply it to a donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: Built-in holiness, where the animal itself is holy (like a kosher בכור)
'But isn't it…?' This opens a challenge

phrases.english: But when this verse is written,
phrases.notes: 'This verse' is הזכרים לה׳, which the ברייתא just quoted for the twin donkeys.

phrases.english: isn't it written about an animal with built-in holiness!
phrases.notes: He means a kosher firstborn, which is itself holy. A firstborn donkey is not holy that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כִּי כְּתִיב הַאי, בִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף הוּא דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the ברייתא in Step 20 could apply a kosher-animal verse to donkeys.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of הזכרים לה׳ for twin donkeys
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse speaks of animals with קדושת הגוף. Donkeys lack that holiness, so the verse should not apply to them. This is also exactly what אביי argued in Step 18.

steps.title: The plural word 'males' teaches a general rule
steps.stepSummary: The verse is about kosher animals, but because it says 'the males' in plural, רבי יוסי הגלילי learns that two can be firstborn, and he extends that to donkeys too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because it says 'The males shall be the Lord's.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the ברייתא is not saying donkeys have built-in holiness. It is using the verse only to learn that two births can both count as first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural word הזכרים shows that two males can both be a בכור at once. רבי יוסי הגלילי treats this as a general fact about firstborns, not something tied to holiness. So he applies it to פטר חמור as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals a corrected understanding
Because it is stated (in the פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a donkey becomes holy. It only borrows the idea that two can be firstborn from the verse.

phrases.english: Rather, because it is stated: 'The males shall be the Lord's,'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves Step 21 by explaining how the verse can teach about donkeys.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of how the verse is being used
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse only works for animals with קדושת הגוף, so donkeys are excluded.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plural הזכרים teaches a general rule that two can be firstborn, and it applies to donkeys too.

steps.title: אביי is firmly refuted
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יוסי הגלילי applies the two-firstborn rule to donkeys, the משנה cannot follow him, and אביי's defense is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of אביי, a full refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion: the ברייתא proves אביי wrong, so the משנה follows the רבנן and not רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי claimed רבי יוסי הגלילי's two-firstborn rule was limited to kosher animals (Step 18). The ברייתא shows he applies it to donkeys too. So the משנה, which does not give both donkeys to the כהן, cannot match his view.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation. The opinion is disproven

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה follows the רבנן: two births cannot happen at exactly the same moment. אביי's attempt to fit it to רבי יוסי הגלילי fails, because רבי יוסי הגלילי applies הזכרים to donkeys too.

phrases.english: The refutation of Abaye is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final result from Steps 20 and 22 against אביי's claim in Step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי is refuted. The משנה is not like רבי יוסי הגלילי, since he applies the two-firstborn rule to donkeys too.
